case: SQLite STRICT ANY table/grid CSV export and import
baseline: Before the tagged encoding, native INTEGER 42, REAL -0.0 and BLOB 00ff80 re-imported as TEXT. Numeric-looking TEXT was indistinguishable from INTEGER; empty TEXT and SQL NULL required an explicit marker.
contract: Versioned per-cell tags preserve SQLite INTEGER, REAL, TEXT and BLOB runtime classes across table-based CSV export/import.
Empty TEXT remains distinct from SQL NULL with an explicit collision-free NULL marker.
Text resembling a tag or formula survives exactly; legacy untagged fields remain TEXT.
Malformed reserved tags and blank cells without an explicit NULL marker are refused during planning before any write.
outcome: Exact text fallback: a versioned engine-specific cell representation is reconstructed using destination metadata declaring ANY, then written through SQLite's typed native bindings.

reproduction.result: Failed before the change: INTEGER, REAL and BLOB values were restored as TEXT; numeric-looking TEXT and INTEGER both became TEXT.

independent_oracle: Native SQLite typeof(value) and returned Value after importing into a separate STRICT ANY table; source and target use SqliteDriver.

focused_app.command: rtk cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-app --lib sqlite_any_contract -- --test-threads=1

clippy.command: rtk cargo clippy --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-core -p tablepro-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings

validation.format_and_diff_checks: cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed

remaining: SQLite arbitrary query results currently expose result-column metadata as NULL for a declared STRICT ANY column; query-result CSV cannot identify the declared ANY type and remains open.
SQLite's existing REAL bound-value refusal for negative zero remains in force; this case verifies representable REAL values only.
Other SQLite storage-class/affinity mixtures, output formats beyond CSV and installed GTK behavior remain open.
This case does not close B3 or qualify the 0.2.0 release.
